ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are Structure A and Structure B. Structure B is located on the right side, the central atom is S, connected around it to four O atoms; in the diagram, the upper and lower S–O are drawn as double bonds, and the left and right S–O are drawn as single bonds. Reasoning: This drawing of Structure B is only one resonance form of this sulfur tetraoxide structure. The double bonds can equivalently be placed between any two oxygen atoms and sulfur, therefore there are multiple equivalent resonance contributing structures. Since the four oxygen atoms are equivalent in the whole resonance system, the real structure does not fixedly contain two single bonds and two double bonds, but is a resonance hybrid. Therefore all S–O bonds are identical to one another.
